walkthroughs.body_html:
Legal Moral & Ethical Issues — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Legal Moral & Ethical Issues brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Legal Moral & Ethical Issues.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Gaining unauthorised access to computer material is an offence under which UK law?
options: Data Protection Act 2018
Computer Misuse Act 1990
Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988
Freedom of Information Act 2000

mcqs.q: Under UK data protection law, individuals have the right to:
options: Access the personal data an organisation holds about them
Delete any company's entire database
Read other customers' records
Ignore copyright on data they download

mcqs.q: Open-source software differs from proprietary software because its:
options: Source code is available to view, modify and redistribute under the licence terms
Use is always completely unregulated
Source code is kept secret by the publisher
Licence forbids anyone from studying the code

mcqs.q: Which of these is primarily an ETHICAL issue rather than a legal one?
options: Hacking into a company server
Selling pirated copies of software
Bias in an algorithm used to shortlist job applicants
Stealing a laptop containing personal data

mcqs.q: If something is legal, is it automatically ethical?
options: Yes - copyright only applies after a patent is granted.
Yes - the law defines exactly what is right and wrong.
Yes - ethics is just the informal name for the legal system.
No - law sets a minimum standard; actions such as exploiting data in ways users never expected can be lawful yet still widely judged unethical.

mcqs.q: Must software be registered before it is protected by copyright?
options: Yes - unregistered software has no copyright protection.
Yes - ethics is just the informal name for the legal system.
Yes - copyright only applies after a patent is granted.
No - in the UK copyright arises automatically when an original work, including source code, is created; no registration is required.

mcqs.q: Does data protection law prevent organisations from storing any personal data?
options: Yes - holding personal data about customers is illegal.
No - it permits processing personal data when there is a lawful basis such as consent or contract, and it imposes duties like security and accuracy.
Yes - ethics is just the informal name for the legal system.
Yes - only the government may store personal data.
